A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Spectral Policy Optimization (SPO) to Stepwise Guided Policy Optimization (SGPO). Their readable main text, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original offline and online LLM training experiments in Tables 2–5 and stylized-model simulations in Appendix C.4.

after.justification: V2 retains original training results and simulations and adds judge-model, voting, ablation and training-dynamics results.

M1.justification: The RTS-based reward, logistic transformation and GRPO update remain unchanged under the rename. V2 adds an evaluated majority-voting option over repeated first-error judgments. V1 only suggested a different minimum-score ensemble as future work in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use LIMO and AIME1997–2023 for training and retain the same nine mathematical evaluation benchmarks, plus LIMO training-set results. The abstract's change from ten benchmarks to nine does not correspond to an actual dataset or task removal.

E2.justification: Matched online experiments retain GRPO and untuned-model comparators, while offline experiments retain positive-only RL. The additional policy backbone and judge variants change configurations and ablations. PRMs and knowledge distillation receive expanded discussion but are not added as evaluated competing training methods.

E3.justification: V2 reports 8192-token rollouts, groups of eight and 32 H200 GPUs for 32B models, versus 4096 tokens, groups of four and eight H200 GPUs in v1. It adds QwQ-32B and four-judgment voting experiments and drops the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct experiment. The revised settings do not establish that the retained, numerically identical 32B results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds judge-strength and beta/gamma ablations, majority-voting tests, pass@16 solved-question overlap analysis, an AIME judge-failure example, and reward/entropy training trajectories in Section 4.3 and Appendix B. These substantially expand analysis beyond the retained positive-versus-negative training comparison and stylized simulations.

E5.justification: V1 Table 5 already reports means and standard deviations over unspecified multiple independent runs. V2 Table 3 explicitly specifies four independent runs for its new 7B judge experiments, but Tables 3–4 do not explicitly define their ± statistic. This does not establish an increase in runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: The original offline results and four original online-model blocks retain their numerical values. V2 adds judge, QwQ-32B, voting, pass@16 and training-dynamics results; for example, its new QwQ-32B comparison reports overall scores of 79.15 for GRPO and 80.17 for SGPO. V1's Qwen2.5-7B results and 8B repeated-run table are removed.

T1.justification: V1 Theorem 3.2 guarantees optimal-policy superiority only once the SPO second-step probability exceeds 31/32. V2 Theorem 3.3 extends the guarantee to every iteration k ≥ 1 under the retained simplified setting. Appendix C replaces the local bound with broader lemmas and a symbolic polynomial argument documented in Table 6.

C1.justification: The central contribution of learning from all-negative groups remains. V2 strengthens the learning-acceleration claim and adds explicit central claims that SGPO works with weaker judges and does not require judges to generate correct solutions, distinguishing it from knowledge distillation in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V2 attributes reliability to reference-based verification and reward scaling, interprets pass@16 gains as learning previously unsolved problems, and links entropy decay to faster convergence. V1's explicit limitations discussion is removed, including its all-positive-group limitation and discussion of stochastic and more general reasoning settings, although simplifying assumptions remain stated.

D1.justification: V2 removes Appendix D's complete character-indexed judge prompt and the model-release access link, losing important information for reproducing the central judging procedure. It adds batched-judging timing of 90 seconds and approximately 10% overhead, references to verl defaults and the LIMO evaluation script, and revised hardware documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on stepwise judges, including StepWiser and RL Tango, knowledge distillation, PRM-guided search and entropy dynamics. It expands distinctions from PRMs and distillation, while retaining most existing literature discussion. Relocation and conversion to author-year citations are presentation changes.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting accompanies the SPO-to-SGPO rename. Experiments are reorganized into offline, online, ablation and discussion sections; related work is consolidated in Appendix A; and the dedicated limitations section and prompt appendix are removed.

P2.justification: V2 removes the pipeline schematic and configuration table, expands and reformats the main results table, and adds ablation/overlap tables, reward/entropy plots and a lengthy proof-coefficient table. The original simulation survives as Figure 4, with one panel also redisplayed in Figure 1. Typography and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the central framework: Appendix C addresses v1's stated local-to-global theoretical gap, while controlled judge, scaling and voting experiments directly investigate feedback reliability previously left largely to future work. These gains outweigh the loss of the exact prompt, release information and some auxiliary results and limitations. Those losses, together with the unexplained 32B setting revision, nevertheless weaken transparency and reproducibility.
